caption: $8=2^3$ has three prime factors with multiplicity, so $-1$
$9=3^2$ has an even count of prime factors, so $+1$
Big integer input is factored exactly
Threads over a list, giving the signs of $(-1)^{\Omega(n)}$
Completely multiplicative, even for non-coprime factors ($162=6\cdot27$)
$60=2^2\cdot3\cdot5$ has four prime factors counted with multiplicity

Two distinct primes multiply the signs to $+1$
Over the divisors of a perfect square the sum is $1$
For a non-square the divisor sum is $0$
